verdicts.title: Two load-best-model checkpoint-correctness tests skip themselves exactly when the behaviour they guard is broken
verdicts.reasoning: Verified every link myself in the current tree. packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_checkpoint_correctness.py:167 `pytest.skip("Eval never improved; nothing to compare.")` guarded by `if trainer.state.best_model_checkpoint is None`, :174 `pytest.skip(f"Expected adapter weights under {best_dir} not found")` guarded by a missing adapter_model.safetensors, and :284 `pytest.skip("Eval never improved; nothing to verify.")` guarded by `if trainer.state.best_global_step is None`. Those are the only three pytest.skip calls in the file. Each guard is the exact observable symptom of the regression the enclosing test exists to catch: TestLoadBestModelMutates asserts that save_model() after load_best_model_at_end writes the best weights (needs best_model_checkpoint + its adapter file), and TestBestFolderLookup::test_best_folder_lookup asserts that best_model_checkpoint resolves to checkpoint-<best_global_step> (needs best_global_step). A trainer change that stops recording a best checkpoint turns both assertions into green skips. Ran the two classes at HEAD with the repo venv: `3 passed, 11 deselected in 7.88s`, so the guards are unreachable today (the first eval always improves over a None best_metric in these deterministic 4-step fixtures) - i.e. dead code that only wakes up to hide a failure. Not a duplicate of an existing issue: Bazalt #774 'Close CI fail-open gates and restore test integrity' is the right umbrella but all of its children are closed, so this instance is untracked. No privacy impact; sibling test test_best_metric_forces_checkpoint_at_intermediate_eval_step in the same class already asserts unconditionally (`assert trainer.state.best_global_step == 2`), which both proves the assertion form is viable and limits the blast radius to the two skipping tests.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Latent test-integrity defect, no runtime or privacy effect today. In packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_checkpoint_correctness.py the guards at lines 167, 174 and 284 are currently unreachable (both classes pass at HEAD: 3 passed in 7.9s, and the first eval necessarily improves over a None best_metric in these 4-step fixtures). If a future DPTrainer change leaves state.best_model_checkpoint or state.best_global_step unset, TestLoadBestModelMutates::test_save_model_after_load_best_sees_best_weights and TestBestFolderLookup::test_best_folder_lookup both report skipped instead of failed, removing the only coverage that save_model() after load_best_model_at_end=True writes the best adapter weights and that the best-checkpoint folder lookup resolves to checkpoint-<best_global_step>. Fix: turn all three preconditions into asserts, as the sibling test test_best_metric_forces_checkpoint_at_intermediate_eval_step in the same file already does.

verdicts.title: LLM fine-tuning tutorial publishes epsilon 1.09 for an adaptively-clipped run whose accounted cost with the mandated adaclip wrapper is 8.99
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. docs/tutorials/llm_finetuning.ipynb cell 11 builds the gradient function with `adaptive_clipped_grad(..., initial_clipping_norm=CLIP_NORM, target_quantile=0.80, clipping_norm_min=0.01, clipping_norm_max=10.0, key=key(0), normalize_by=BATCH_SIZE)` and never passes fraction_noise_std, so it takes the 0.05 default (_DEFAULT_FRACTION_NOISE_STD in packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:27); _sample_noisy_clipping_rate in the same file adds Gaussian noise to the clipping rate and _adaptive_clipping_norm_update consumes it every step, so a noisy quantile statistic is genuinely released each of the 20 steps (the stored outputs show the threshold moving: clip=0.013 -> 0.027). Both the pre-computation in cell 11 and the per-step tracker in cell 13 price the run as `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(NOISE_MULTIPLIER), sample_rate, truncated_batch_size=MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dataset_size=len(train_dataset)) * steps` - plain Gaussian, no adaclip wrapper. `grep -ic adaclip docs/tutorials/llm_finetuning.ipynb` = 0, and no markdown cell mentions the extra cost; it is the only tutorial that uses adaptive clipping (adaptive_clipped_grad appears in llm_finetuning.ipynb only). The repo's own guidance is the opposite: docs/user-guide/clipping.md:230-249 'Adaptive clipping introduces an additional privacy cost (the noisy clipping rate query). Account for it using dpsgd_acc.adaclip()', and examples/train_dpsgd.py builds the adaclip chain. Measured with the repo venv at the notebook's own constants (nm=1.5, sample_rate=8/500, truncated_batch_size=12, dataset_size=500, 20 steps, delta=1e-5): notebook chain = 1.0944 (matches the published 'Expected final epsilon: 1.09' and 'Final: ... epsilon=1.09'); same chain with dpsgd_acc.adaclip(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.5), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=8) as inner = 8.9928, an 8.2x understatement. The notebook is not executed in CI (.github/workflows/pr.yml:295-297 runs only accounting_and_calibration, dp_sgd_training, dp_ftrl_training), and executing it would not catch this since the wrong chain runs cleanly. Direction is optimistic (understated epsilon) in a published artifact, hence high rather than low; not a code defect, so not critical.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: docs/tutorials/llm_finetuning.ipynb trains with adaptive clipping (fraction_noise_std at its 0.05 default, so a noisy clip-rate query is released on each of the 20 steps and visibly moves the threshold from 0.013 to 0.027) but reports privacy with the plain Gaussian + truncated-Poisson chain in cells 11 and 13, and ships the resulting number in its stored outputs ('Expected final epsilon: 1.09', 'Final: loss=6.752, epsilon=1.09'). Re-measured at the notebook's constants (nm=1.5, q=8/500, truncated_batch_size=12, dataset_size=500, 20 steps, delta=1e-5): the notebook chain gives 1.0944, while wrapping the inner mechanism in dpsgd_acc.adaclip(..., fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=8) - the form docs/user-guide/clipping.md:230-249 mandates for exactly this configuration - gives 8.9928. A reader who copies the tutorial's accounting line into their own adaptive-clipping run therefore reports an epsilon roughly 8x below what their mechanism provides. The notebook is absent from the pr.yml notebook-execution list, and executing it would not surface the error because the wrong chain runs without complaint.

verdicts.title: dpftrl_acc.poisson's sample_rate is the per-active-band conditional rate, but the accounting reference and user guide never say so
verdicts.reasoning: The semantics claim and the documentation gap both hold; the stated failure mechanism and its 104x magnitude are overstated, so I downgraded high -> medium and rewrote the scenario. Verified: CyclicPoissonSampler's sample_rate is the inclusion probability within the active group (module docstring packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/sampling/_poisson.py:1-20 'Step i activates only group i % bands; each example in that group is included independently with probability sample_rate', and the class Note 'Expected batch size per step is |group| * sample_rate where |group| = |D| / bands'), and CyclicPoisson in packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:50-54 must be given that same conditional rate ('BandMF requires cyclic sampling over fixed dataset partitions; sample_rate is conditional on the active partition'). packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:130-163 (_cyclic_poisson_group_rate) converts a global rate by local_size/group_size ~ bands before calling the accountant, confirming the conditional reading. The docs gap is real: docs/reference/accounting.md:468 says only '- sample_rate (float): Poisson sampling probability per round.', and docs/user-guide/accounting.md's dpftrl_acc.poisson section, docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md, and docs/index.md all show band_mf_strategy(bands=10)/bands=64 with a bare sample_rate=0.01 and never mention the per-band conversion; the only correct statement in the docs tree is the Tips bullet at docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:321-325. Where the finding overreaches: the reference never actually says 'whole-dataset', it is silent, and every place in the repo that pairs a sampler with this accountant uses ONE variable for both (docs/tutorials/dp_ftrl_training.ipynb line 152 'sample_rate = batch_size * bands / n_samples'; examples/train_dpftrl.py:1224 sampling_prob = batch*bands/N passed to both CyclicPoissonSampler and dpftrl_acc.poisson). Passing a global q consistently to sampler and accountant is mathematically sound - it just realizes a batch bands x smaller than intended, a utility bug, not a privacy bug. The privacy understatement requires the user to feed the accountant a different number than the sampler. I did reproduce the magnitude of that mismatch: bands=10, n_steps=1000, nm=1.0, delta=1e-5 -> q=0.01 gives eps 0.71807 and q=0.1 gives eps 7.04689 (9.8x), and nothing validates the rate because q_global < q_conditional is always in (0,1]. Not a duplicate: Bazalt #775/#845 cover citation verification, not this parameter's semantics.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Documentation gap on a privacy-critical parameter, no code defect. dpftrl_acc.poisson's sample_rate must be the per-active-band conditional inclusion probability (~bands x the whole-dataset rate), as CyclicPoissonSampler's docstring and DPTrainer's _cyclic_poisson_group_rate both show, but docs/reference/accounting.md:468 documents it only as 'Poisson sampling probability per round' and the worked examples in docs/user-guide/accounting.md, docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md and docs/index.md pass a bare sample_rate=0.01 alongside bands=10/64 with no conversion; the correct statement lives only in docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:321-325. A reader who applies the DP-SGD convention q = expected_batch_size / dataset_size consistently to both sampler and accountant is still soundly accounted - the realized batch is simply bands x smaller than intended (utility, not privacy). The privacy exposure appears only if the reader then fixes the sampler to the conditional rate (to recover the intended batch size) while leaving the global rate in the accountant: nothing validates the pairing, since q_global < q_conditional always passes the (0,1] check. Measured cost of that mismatch at the docs' own bands=10 / n_steps=1000 / nm=1.0 / delta=1e-5 configuration: q=0.01 reports eps 0.718 where q=0.1 is the truth at eps 7.047, a 9.8x understatement.

verdicts.title: Sampling reference denies CyclicPoissonSampler's truncated_batch_size and contradicts the class docstring rendered on the same page
verdicts.reasoning: Every mechanical claim reproduced. docs/reference/sampling.md:193-196 reads 'account with dpftrl_acc.poisson(mechanism, sample_rate, n_steps=...). There is no batch-size cap on this sampler; dpftrl_acc.poisson matches uncapped Poisson draws only.' Both halves are false at HEAD: inspect.signature(CyclicPoissonSampler.__init__) = (self, data_source, sample_rate, bands=1, n_steps=1, partition_type=PartitionType.EQUAL_SPLIT, truncated_batch_size: int | None = None, *, key), and inspect.signature(opaque.dpftrl.accounting.poisson) = (inner, sample_rate, *, n_steps, truncated_batch_size=None, dataset_size=None). The parameter tables at docs/reference/sampling.md:184-190 and docs/user-guide/sampling.md:164-172 both omit truncated_batch_size, while the mkdocstrings directive on the same reference page (::: opaque.dpftrl.sampling.CyclicPoissonSampler, docs/reference/sampling.md:258) renders the class docstring, which documents the cap and its identity-only accounting restriction - so the rendered page contradicts itself. Executed the cap: CyclicPoissonSampler(range(1000), sample_rate=0.5, bands=4, n_steps=20, truncated_batch_size=60, key=key(0)) constructs without complaint and yields 60 for all 20 batches, where the same sampler without the cap yields 112-136. dpftrl_acc.poisson refuses that configuration (ConfigurationError 'truncated Poisson is only supported for IdentityStrategy inner (BandMfStrategy per-group truncation is not implemented)'), so a bands>1 capped sampler has no matching accountant; the trainer path is fail-closed (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:229-236 rejects truncated_batch_size under sampling_mode='cyclic_poisson'), leaving the direct library surface as the only exposure. Pricing a capped sampler with the plain-Poisson PLD is optimistic: measured the DP-SGD analogue at nm=1.1, q=0.032, dataset_size=1000, 500 steps, delta=1e-5 -> plain 3.8333 vs truncated 15.7361 (4.1x; the finding's 9.2359 figure did not reproduce at the config I used, the direction and rough magnitude did). Medium is right: a docs falsehood plus a constructible-but-unaccountable sampler configuration, reachable only by hand-rolled library code, not by the trainer or by any default.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: docs/reference/sampling.md:193-196 states that CyclicPoissonSampler has no batch-size cap and that dpftrl_acc.poisson matches uncapped Poisson draws only. Both are false: the sampler takes truncated_batch_size (verified: bands=4, sample_rate=0.5, truncated_batch_size=60 constructs silently and returns exactly 60 examples on all 20 steps, versus 112-136 uncapped), and dpftrl_acc.poisson takes truncated_batch_size/dataset_size for an IdentityStrategy inner. The same reference page renders the class docstring below via mkdocstrings, which documents the cap, so the page contradicts itself, and both parameter tables (docs/reference/sampling.md:184-190, docs/user-guide/sampling.md:164-172) omit the parameter. Consequences: (a) a reader never learns the truncated form of dpftrl_acc.poisson exists for identity MF, and (b) a hand-rolled bands>1 run can cap its batches while dpftrl_acc.poisson rejects the matching truncated accounting (ConfigurationError, BandMF per-group truncation unimplemented), leaving only the plain-Poisson PLD, which is optimistic for a capped sampler - measured in the DP-SGD analogue as 3.83 vs 15.74 epsilon at nm=1.1, q=0.032, 500 steps, delta=1e-5. DPTrainer refuses the combination outright, so no default or trainer-driven configuration is affected.
